request.spec:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each claim its status log: one line per status it has had, oldest first, as
<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>, where the date is the sheet's today when the change was
made and the due is the claim's due as it was computed at that moment (including the DRAFT line
written when the claim was added).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each claim now shows its status log, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

Each line reads `<STATUS> by <user> on <date> due=<due>`, oldest first. The DRAFT line is written when the claim is added, and another line each time its status changes. The date is the sheet's today at that moment. The due is the claim's due exactly as its row showed it then, including the floor, any statement figure, any late charge, or the fixed due once settled. A due with no figure shows as `n/a`.

What changed:

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V28__claim_log.sql`, adds a `claim_log` table with one entry per status a claim has had.
- **Server:**
  - A new `ClaimLogRepository` writes an entry and builds the lines. It works out the due with the same `Dues.shown` the screen's figures are based on, so the two can't disagree.
  - An entry is written when a claim is added (through the claim form or quick-add), when its status changes (open, settle, approve, reject, void, or a clerk's settle that becomes PENDING), and when bulk open opens it.
  - Entries are written in the same transaction as the change, so a refused change logs nothing.
  - The claims list now returns each claim's `log`.
- **Front end:** each claim row lists its lines as `claim-log-line` items inside a `claim-log` list.

Editing a claim or moving it to another person adds no line, because neither changes its status. That matches what the tests expect.

Claims that existed before this change start with an empty log, because their history was never recorded.
